skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

skills.name: ast-consistency
skills.description: AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged.

skills.name: body-removal
skills.description: Remove function bodies from Rust/Verus source files to produce signature-only views. Used before the view-design phase to prevent implementation anchoring.

skills.name: bug-reporting
skills.description: Classify and report bugs found during Verus verification. Distinguishes true bugs from missing constraints and verifier limitations. Use when a verification failure might indicate a code bug.

skills.name: caller-analysis
skills.description: Analyze callers of a Rust module to understand usage expectations for Verus verification. Produces a caller-perspective analysis covering all functions with their visibility and call relationships.

skills.name: crate-analysis
skills.description: Principles for verification order in multi-file Rust crates. Verify leaf modules first so downstream modules can reference upstream specs directly. The pipeline tool handles ordering automatically.

skills.name: proof-extraction
skills.description: Extract large inline proof blocks from exec code into named lemmas in .proof.rs. Use when polishing verified code to improve readability and proof organization.

skills.name: proof-minimization
skills.description: Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity.

skills.name: property-analysis
skills.description: How to analyze source code and identify verification properties — the WHAT of verification. Covers module understanding, property discovery across four dimensions (functional correctness, safety, liveness, structural consistency), and quality review. Use this skill when deciding what to verify for a new module, writing property_analysis.md, or updating global_properties.md.

skills.name: proving-guide
skills.description: Proving methodology and mindset for Verus verification: function-by-function approach, persistence through failures, clean verification, and bug reporting. Use when writing proofs or resolving verification failures.

skills.name: review-methodology
skills.description: Review Verus verification code with focus on spec quality and automated checks.

skills.name: spec-completeness
skills.description: Detect specification incompleteness via nondeterminism checking. Given a Verus function spec, automatically determine whether the spec uniquely determines the output for each valid input. If not, use type-guided binary search to construct a concrete witness (input + two valid but different outputs). No LLM needed — pure SMT-based.

skills.name: spec-design
skills.description: How to write good Verus specs. Covers spec quality principles (anti-patterns, error paths), spec classification (internal, external-top, external-bottom trust boundaries), View abstraction design, and static vs dynamic enforcement. Use when writing or reviewing Verus specs.

skills.name: verus-constraints
skills.description: Mandatory rules for writing Verus code. Covers attribute-based syntax, source integrity for exec code, forbidden patterns, and assume_specification policy. Must be followed whenever producing or modifying Verus-annotated code.

skills.name: verus-setup
skills.description: Set up Verus formal verification infrastructure for a Rust project. Covers workspace-level config (vstd dependency, cfg flags, version pinning, Makefile, scripts) and per-crate config (metadata, cfg-gated includes, spec/proof stubs). Use this skill when preparing a repo or crate for Verus verification, adding make verify support, or integrating cheating detection into a build.

skills.name: verus-syntax
skills.description: Verus attribute-based syntax reference for exec functions. Covers #[verus_spec], #[verus_verify], proof!{}, proof_decl!{}, loop invariants. See GUIDE.md for advanced patterns, syntax_attr.rs for the official example.

skills.name: view-design
skills.description: How to design a View type that represents abstract state from the caller's perspective. Input: caller analysis + property concepts. Must NOT see implementation code.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings.

1. ## Response to Turn 1
2. 
3. ### Goal
4. Remove `external_body` from `Cache::new` (Step 4 of the reviewer's drill-down: rewrite + add `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new`).
5. 
6. ### Attempt 1: Direct `impl View for BTreeMap` + `assume_specification`
7. - Changes: Added `impl View for alloc::collections::BTreeMap<K, V>` in `lib.spec.rs`, plus `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new` with `m@ == Map::empty()`. Removed `external_body` from `Cache::new`.
8. - Result: **FAILED** — Rust orphan rule (`E0117`): cannot implement foreign trait `View` on foreign type `BTreeMap` in a downstream crate.
9. 
10. ### Attempt 2: Proxy type `ExBTreeMap` with View + `assume_specification`
11. - Changes: Implemented `View` on the existing `ExBTreeMap` proxy type, wrote `assume_specification` returning `ExBTreeMap`.
12. - Result: **FAILED** — `E0308` type mismatch: Rust treats `ExBTreeMap` and `BTreeMap` as different types despite `external_type_specification`.
13. 
14. ### Attempt 3: `assume_specification` without View (no `m@`)
15. - Changes: Added `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new` with no View-based ensures. Removed `external_body`. Cache View remained `uninterp`.
16. - Result: **FAILED** — Postcondition failures: `result@ == CacheView::spec_new(...)` and `result@.inv()` both unprovable because View is uninterpreted. This confirmed the reviewer's expected outcome for step 4.
17. 
18. ### Attempt 4: Custom `btreemap_view_spec` + interpreted Cache View
19. - Changes: Created `pub uninterp spec fn btreemap_view_spec<K,V>(m: BTreeMap<K,V>) -> Map<K,V>` to avoid orphan rules. Rewrote `assume_specification` to use `btreemap_view_spec(m) == Map::empty()`. Created `cache_contents_of` and `cache_lru_of` helper spec functions connecting BTreeMap fields to CacheView. Changed Cache View from `uninterp` to interpreted body using these helpers.
20. - Sub-attempts for visibility issues:
21.   - **4a**: `open spec fn` helpers → error: `open` requires `pub`
22.   - **4b**: Made helpers `pub` → error: `btreemap_view_spec` private in public ensures
23.   - **4c**: Made `btreemap_view_spec` `pub` → error: `pub open cache_contents_of` accesses private `CacheEntry`
24.   - **4d**: Made helpers non-pub `spec fn` (closed) → error: `pub open` Cache View can't call private functions
25.   - **4e**: Made Cache View `closed spec fn` → **COMPILED!** 11 verified, 1 error: `result@.inv()` postcondition fails (needs reveal of closed functions in proof)
26. 
27. ### Attempt 5: `proof!` block with inline `reveal`
28. - Changes: Added `proof! { reveal(<Cache<K,V> as View>::view); ... }` in `Cache::new` body.
29. - Result: **FAILED** — `E0401`: can't use generic parameters `K`, `V` from outer item in `proof!` (which expands to a nested function).
30. 
31. ### Attempt 6: Proof lemma as associated function (bitmap crate pattern)
32. - Changes: Created `lemma_new_view` as `proof fn` inside `impl<K: Ord + Clone, V> Cache<K, V>` block in `lib.proof.rs`. Called from `Cache::new` via `proof! { Self::lemma_new_view(&result, capacity); }`.
33. - Sub-attempts for `reveal` syntax:
34.   - **6a**: `reveal(<Self as View>::view)` → error: "Self is not supported in reveal/hide"
35.   - **6b**: `reveal(<Cache<K, V> as View>::view)` → error: `E0401` again (K, V from outer impl block)
36.   - **6c**: `reveal(<Cache<_, _> as View>::view)` → **SUCCESS!** 13 verified, 0 errors.
37. 
38. ### Final Result
39. - Status: **FIXED**
40. - `external_body` count on user functions: was 7 → now **6** (removed from `Cache::new`)
41. - Total `external_body` count reported by guardrails: 8 (includes `ExBTreeMap` external type spec + `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new`, which are infrastructure, not user functions)
42. - Verification: **13 verified, 0 errors**
43. 
44. ### Changes Made
45. 
46. **`lib.rs`** (lines 146–156):
47. - Removed `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` from `Cache::new`
48. - Changed body from direct struct return to `let result = Self {...}; proof! { Self::lemma_new_view(&result, capacity); } result`
49. 
50. **`lib.spec.rs`** (lines 29–69, 216–226):
51. - Added `btreemap_view_spec<K,V>` — uninterpreted spec function mirroring vstd's `View::view` for BTreeMap (orphan rules prevent implementing the trait directly)
52. - Added `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new` with ensures `btreemap_view_spec(m) == Map::empty()`
53. - Added `cache_contents_of<K,V>` — closed spec fn projecting BTreeMap contents to `Map<K,V>` via `CacheEntry::value`
54. - Added `cache_lru_of<K,V>` — closed spec fn with interpreted empty case (`Seq::empty()` when domain is empty) and uninterpreted non-empty case
55. - Changed Cache `View::view` from `uninterp` to `closed spec fn` with interpreted body using the helpers above
56. 
57. **`lib.proof.rs`** (lines 320–351):
58. - Added `impl<K: Ord + Clone, V> Cache<K, V>` block with `lemma_new_view` proof function
59. - Uses `reveal(<Cache<_, _> as View>::view)`, `reveal(cache_contents_of)`, `reveal(cache_lru_of)` to expose closed function bodies
60. - Proves `result@.contents =~= Map::empty()` and `result@.lru_order == Seq::empty()`
61. 
62. ### Trust Boundary
63. The `assume_specification` for `BTreeMap::new` is a new trust assumption — it axiomatizes that a freshly created BTreeMap is empty. This matches vstd's own spec at `vstd/std_specs/btree.rs:613-616` and is required because vstd's BTreeMap specs are gated behind `cfg(std)`, unavailable on this no_std kernel target. This must be documented in `trust.md`.
64.

83. // CacheView - Abstract Specification Model
84. //==================================================================================================
85. 
86. /// Abstract view of a bounded LRU cache.
87. ///
88. /// - `contents`: the key-value mapping of all cached entries.
89. /// - `capacity`: maximum number of entries.
90. /// - `lru_order`: keys ordered from LRU (index 0) to MRU (last element).
91. #[verifier::ext_equal]
92. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(K)]
93. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(V)]
94. pub struct CacheView<K, V> {
95.     pub contents: Map<K, V>,
96.     pub capacity: nat,
97.     pub lru_order: Seq<K>,
98. }
99. 
100. impl<K, V> CacheView<K, V> {
101. 
102.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
103.     // Well-formedness Invariant
104.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
105. 
106.     /// Well-formedness invariant for the abstract cache state.
107.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
108.         // Size never exceeds capacity.
109.         &&& self.contents.dom().len() <= self.capacity
110.         // LRU order has no duplicates.
111.         &&& self.lru_order.no_duplicates()
112.         // LRU order contains exactly the stored keys.
113.         &&& self.lru_order.to_set() == self.contents.dom()
114.         // Explicit cardinality link (helps the solver).
115.         &&& self.lru_order.len() == self.contents.dom().len()
116.     }
117. 
118.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
119.     // Helper Spec Functions
120.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
121. 
122.     /// Move `key` to the most-recently-used position (end of the sequence).
123.     /// Preserves all other elements and their relative order.
124.     pub open spec fn move_to_mru(self, key: K) -> Seq<K> {
125.         self.lru_order.filter(|k: K| k != key).push(key)
126.     }
127. 
128.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
129.     // Spec Transition Functions
130.     //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
131. 
132.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::new`.
133.     pub open spec fn spec_new(capacity: nat) -> CacheView<K, V> {
134.         CacheView {
135.             contents: Map::empty(),
136.             capacity,
137.             lru_order: Seq::empty(),
138.         }
139.     }
140. 
141.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::get`.
142.     /// Returns the updated cache state and the lookup result.
143.     pub open spec fn spec_get(self, key: K) -> (CacheView<K, V>, Option<V>) {
144.         if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
145.             (CacheView {
146.                 lru_order: self.move_to_mru(key),
147.                 ..self
148.             }, Some(self.contents[key]))
149.         } else {
150.             (self, None)
151.         }
152.     }
153. 
154.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::put`.
155.     pub open spec fn spec_put(self, key: K, value: V) -> CacheView<K, V> {
156.         if self.capacity == 0 {
157.             // Zero-capacity cache: no-op.
158.             self
159.         } else if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
160.             // Overwrite existing key: replace value, refresh recency.
161.             CacheView {
162.                 contents: self.contents.insert(key, value),
163.                 lru_order: self.move_to_mru(key),
164.                 ..self
165.             }
166.         } else if self.contents.dom().len() >= self.capacity {
167.             // At capacity with new key: evict LRU victim, then insert.
168.             let victim = self.lru_order[0];
169.             CacheView {
170.                 contents: self.contents.remove(victim).insert(key, value),
171.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.subrange(1, self.lru_order.len() as int).push(key),
172.                 ..self
173.             }
174.         } else {
175.             // Below capacity with new key: insert directly.
176.             CacheView {
177.                 contents: self.contents.insert(key, value),
178.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.push(key),
179.                 ..self
180.             }
181.         }
182.     }
183. 
184.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::remove`.
185.     pub open spec fn spec_remove(self, key: K) -> CacheView<K, V> {
186.         if self.contents.dom().contains(key) {
187.             CacheView {
188.                 contents: self.contents.remove(key),
189.                 lru_order: self.lru_order.filter(|k: K| k != key),
190.                 ..self
191.             }
192.         } else {
193.             // Key absent: no-op.
194.             self
195.         }
196.     }
197. 
198.     /// Spec transition for `Cache::clear`.
199.     pub open spec fn spec_clear(self) -> CacheView<K, V> {
200.         CacheView {
201.             contents: Map::empty(),
202.             lru_order: Seq::empty(),
203.             ..self  // capacity preserved
204.         }
205.     }
206. }
